title: Alpha finding triage record
description: One record per Alpha finding. Section 15 requires a classification, a reproduction, an affected artifact, severity, evidence, an owner and a disposition. The classification vocabulary is closed so that a finding cannot be filed under a label invented to make it less blocking, and the four blocking classes are named in the schema rather than left to a reader's judgement.

findingId.description: Stable for the life of the finding. Reclassification never changes it.

reporter.description: Pseudonymous tester identifier. Never a name, never an email address; the importer redacts before storage.

classificationHistory.description: Every classification this finding has held, appended never rewritten. A finding that turns out to be an instrument defect is reclassified, not deleted.

affectedArtifactDigest.description: The digest of the image the tester actually ran. Not a version string, which two builds can share, and not a branch. Section 14 forbids mixing feedback from multiple artifacts without labelling them, and this field is the label.

reproducible.description: not-reproduced is a real value. A finding nobody could reproduce stays open as not-reproduced rather than being closed as absent.

evidenceClass.description: Kept apart deliberately. Subjective feedback never becomes an objective performance claim, and a tester reporting that something felt fast is not evidence that it was.

environmentMeasurement.description: Required when classification is ENVIRONMENT. An environment classification names what was measured, never what was inferred: a claim about the host carried for a week here once turned out never to have been measured at all.

approvedBy.description: Required for ACCEPTED. A named person, not a role.

x-blockingNote: Blocking condition 9 is unmet while any finding in x-blockingClassifications has disposition.state OPEN. The remaining classifications are recorded and do not block. Zero findings does not satisfy the condition: zero testers means it is unmet, not vacuously met.
